---
title: "Shared-library backend examples"
---

qgsim can orchestrate simulation engines implemented outside R while keeping
the common workflow:

```text
breeding_scheme() -> qgsim_compile() -> qgsim_validate()
                  -> qgsim_run() -> qgsim_result
```

The repository includes two small developer examples. Both keep the qgsim
backend responsibilities separate:

- `translate()` converts a validated `qgsim_plan` to simple native input.
- `execute()` calls a function from a shared library.
- `collect()` converts the native output into a valid `qgsim_result`.

These examples are optional, compiler-dependent developer guidance. They are
not scientifically complete simulators, are not built during qgsim
installation, and are not required by the package test suite.

## C++ shared-library backend

The C++ example uses R's `.Call()` interface. Its native function receives a
numeric vector and adds a generation-specific increment. The accompanying R
script builds a qgsim backend around that toy function and runs it through
`qgsim_run()`.

Source files:

- [`qgsim_cpp_example.cpp`](https://github.com/psoerensen/qgsim/blob/main/inst/examples/cpp_backend/qgsim_cpp_example.cpp):
  the native C++ function.
- [`build.R`](https://github.com/psoerensen/qgsim/blob/main/inst/examples/cpp_backend/build.R):
  builds the shared library with `R CMD SHLIB`.
- [`test_cpp_backend.R`](https://github.com/psoerensen/qgsim/blob/main/inst/examples/cpp_backend/test_cpp_backend.R):
  loads the library, registers the example backend, and runs a small plan.

From `inst/examples/cpp_backend/`, build and run it with:

```bash
Rscript build.R
Rscript test_cpp_backend.R
```

Building requires a C++ compiler configured for R.

## Fortran shared-library backend

The Fortran example uses R's `.Fortran()` interface. Its native subroutine
updates a numeric vector by adding a generation-specific increment. The
accompanying R script keeps the same `translate()`, `execute()`, and
`collect()` structure as the C++ example.

Source files:

- [`qgsim_fortran_example.f90`](https://github.com/psoerensen/qgsim/blob/main/inst/examples/fortran_backend/qgsim_fortran_example.f90):
  the native Fortran subroutine.
- [`build.R`](https://github.com/psoerensen/qgsim/blob/main/inst/examples/fortran_backend/build.R):
  builds the shared library with `R CMD SHLIB`.
- [`test_fortran_backend.R`](https://github.com/psoerensen/qgsim/blob/main/inst/examples/fortran_backend/test_fortran_backend.R):
  loads the library, registers the example backend, and runs a small plan.

From `inst/examples/fortran_backend/`, build and run it with:

```bash
Rscript build.R
Rscript test_fortran_backend.R
```

Building requires a Fortran compiler configured for R.

The scripts use qgsim's internal strict backend and result constructors because
those constructors are not currently part of the public API. A production
backend package should pin compatible qgsim versions and keep this adapter code
isolated.
